title: What would liberation mean?
editorial_thesis: Define the goal before comparing practices
interpretive_constraint: Stop beginning with techniques; first establish what the tradition means by freedom
source_selection_instruction: Locate a source passage where the author distinguishes liberation from mere acquisition

title: Knowledge and ignorance
editorial_thesis: Two kinds of ignorance are not identical
interpretive_constraint: The difference between mistaken judgment and embodied limitation alters what a practice can accomplish
source_selection_instruction: Select from gold āhnika 1 and proof its compound morphology

title: The most immediate entry
editorial_thesis: Do not mistake proximity for ease
interpretive_constraint: The direct approach to recognition needs careful exposition without making a state claim
source_selection_instruction: Choose a verified source on anupāya/śāmbhavopāya

title: The usefulness of means
editorial_thesis: A means works within an actual structure of attention
interpretive_constraint: Avoid ranking practitioners by allegedly superior experiences
source_selection_instruction: Select a verified sequence of upāyas

title: How a world appears
editorial_thesis: Manifestation is an account, not a diagram replacing experience
interpretive_constraint: Explain the root distinction between a principle and the object it classifies
source_selection_instruction: Choose a gold source defining tattva

title: Contraction and differentiation
editorial_thesis: The language of limitation must not imply a cosmic mistake
interpretive_constraint: Name the difference between free manifestation and bound perception
source_selection_instruction: Choose gold āhnika with the relevant māyā analysis

title: The limited subject
editorial_thesis: The individual is not merely a small object
interpretive_constraint: Differentiate āṇu as subject-position from aṇu as dictionary 'minute'
source_selection_instruction: Find a source with explicit aṇu or āṇava language

title: Freedom inside manifestation
editorial_thesis: Do not portray liberation as deletion of the 36 principles
interpretive_constraint: Show how recognition can transform understanding without abolishing perceptual difference
source_selection_instruction: Select gold discussion of the tattva series

title: The body as participant
editorial_thesis: Embodiment must remain concrete
interpretive_constraint: Distinguish body-practice from literary body metaphor
source_selection_instruction: Choose a verified practice instruction with bodily referents

title: The senses are active
editorial_thesis: Sensation is not automatically a distraction
interpretive_constraint: Avoid the false move that every pleasure is already liberation
source_selection_instruction: Select gold discussion of the senses

title: The breath and its intervals
editorial_thesis: Breathing is not a performance of supernatural control
interpretive_constraint: Explain where breath practice sits among the means
source_selection_instruction: Select a verified gold passage with no unlicensed breath retention instruction

title: A locus for attention
editorial_thesis: The body's point can be a location or an image
interpretive_constraint: Do not conflate traditional nyāsa with anatomical fact
source_selection_instruction: Source precise body placement from witness

title: Speech before words
editorial_thesis: Technical vocabulary must not float without grammar
interpretive_constraint: Separate varṇa, mantra and ordinary language
source_selection_instruction: Find gold passage on phonemes and manifestation

title: The first vowel
editorial_thesis: Phonemic symbolism is not phonological derivation
interpretive_constraint: Teach the symbolic status of a only with the commentator's actual wording
source_selection_instruction: Select exact cited line

title: Mantra and the knower
editorial_thesis: Pronunciation alone and recognition are not the same question
interpretive_constraint: Keep theology from becoming an invented etymology
source_selection_instruction: Choose gold mantra passage

title: The alphabet's body
editorial_thesis: Different orders require different witnesses
interpretive_constraint: Do not substitute Mālinī for Mātṛkā without naming the tradition
source_selection_instruction: Use gold body-phoneme passage

title: The circle of powers
editorial_thesis: The diagram is a relation, not a magic map
interpretive_constraint: Describe what is represented and why
source_selection_instruction: Select gold source defining cakra

title: Central and peripheral
editorial_thesis: The middle is a ritual position and a philosophical relation
interpretive_constraint: Avoid an unsupported neural or quantum interpretation
source_selection_instruction: Select sourced mandala passage

title: Appearance as worship
editorial_thesis: The senses can be understood as participants in offering
interpretive_constraint: Distinguish text instruction from modern adaptation
source_selection_instruction: Select exact ritual source

title: The mandala dissolves
editorial_thesis: A construction has a procedure and a completion
interpretive_constraint: Show what a text means by withdrawal without describing a guaranteed experience
source_selection_instruction: Select closing passage

title: What an offering gives
editorial_thesis: An omnipresent deity requires no food
interpretive_constraint: Explain the paradox of giving to the all-pervading without erasing practice
source_selection_instruction: Choose gold offering line

title: Whom is ritual for?
editorial_thesis: The rite does something to a practitioner
interpretive_constraint: Do not claim ritual is useless when a text discusses its transformations
source_selection_instruction: Choose gold instruction with stated purpose

title: The everyday and the initiated
editorial_thesis: Do not conceal ritual prerequisites
interpretive_constraint: Distinguish a householder analogy from restricted initiation procedures
source_selection_instruction: Choose permissible gold passage

title: How a rite ends
editorial_thesis: Dismissal and continuity are both meaningful categories
interpretive_constraint: Avoid treating the end as a failure of nonduality
source_selection_instruction: Choose verified source on concluding ritual

title: Āṇavopāya
editorial_thesis: Embodied practices work with differentiated means
interpretive_constraint: Do not rank this as morally inferior
source_selection_instruction: Choose source with operational definition

title: Śāktopāya
editorial_thesis: Conceptual attention can turn upon itself
interpretive_constraint: Avoid describing it as merely 'thinking harder'
source_selection_instruction: Choose source with precise technical example

title: Śāmbhavopāya
editorial_thesis: A direct movement is not a guaranteed revelation
interpretive_constraint: Interpret immediate will without exotic claims
source_selection_instruction: Choose gold source distinguishing method

title: Anupāya
editorial_thesis: Non-method does not make other methods frauds
interpretive_constraint: State what the text actually allows
source_selection_instruction: Use a source where anupāya is defined

title: What a siddhi claims
editorial_thesis: A traditional claim is not a scientific demonstration
interpretive_constraint: Present contextual meaning and textual genre first
source_selection_instruction: Choose gold power-claims passage

title: Recognition is not a spectacle
editorial_thesis: Avoid promises of visions and bodily signs
interpretive_constraint: Distinguish doctrine from testimony
source_selection_instruction: Select source about fruit/signs

title: The guru and knowledge
editorial_thesis: Transmission does not erase individual critical judgment
interpretive_constraint: Give technical definition only after witness check
source_selection_instruction: Select gold initiation passage

title: Freedom in action
editorial_thesis: Action need not stop when agency is recognised differently
interpretive_constraint: Do not turn this into 'all actions are beyond ethics'
source_selection_instruction: Choose gold reflection on liberated action

title: Who recognises?
editorial_thesis: The subject cannot simply be turned into an object
interpretive_constraint: Distinguish grammatical first person from metaphysical self
source_selection_instruction: Select gold I-consciousness passage

title: What is recognised?
editorial_thesis: Recognition changes the relation of knower and known
interpretive_constraint: Do not claim that difference ceases phenomenologically
source_selection_instruction: Select gold pratyabhijñā passage

title: Freedom and the world
editorial_thesis: Return to manifestation without contempt
interpretive_constraint: Keep nature and moral reality present
source_selection_instruction: Choose a late gold passage on freedom

title: The ordinary after the teaching
editorial_thesis: An accurate ending requires less explanation
interpretive_constraint: Distil the final claim to a sourced paragraph
source_selection_instruction: Select a gold concluding passage
